text: How many T-shirts do you want?
Sorry, we don't have any small sizes.
Hi there! Can I help you?
Yes, please. How much is this T-shirt?
It's twelve dollars. It's very cheap this week. What size do you need?
Medium. Do you have any black ones?
Sorry, we don't have any black ones in medium. We have some red and some white.
White is fine. Two, please. Can I pay in cash?
Sure. Two T-shirts, twenty-four dollars. And here is your change: six dollars.
Thanks! Thirty minus twenty-four, six. That's right.
Do you have any medium sizes?
Excuse me, I think the change is wrong.

Hi Bruno, it's Tyler. I'm at the mall and I need your help. They have some really cool basketball shoes here, but they are expensive: one hundred and twenty dollars. I don't have any cash, only my card, and my mom says the limit is one hundred. So, no shoes today. But the socks are cheap: five dollars for three pairs. How many pairs do you want? I can buy some for you. Oh, and they don't have any caps in your size. Call me back, OK?

Attention, shoppers. Today only, all T-shirts are ten dollars. How many can you take? Up to five per person. Shorts are twenty-five dollars, and caps are on sale for fifteen. We don't have any large sizes in the blue caps, sorry. Please pay at the front of the store. We take cash and cards, and we always give you a receipt. Thank you for shopping with us.

Bruno goes to a sports store on Saturday. He asks how much the T-shirts are. They are cheap, so he takes two. He pays in cash with a fifty-dollar bill. The cashier gives him his change and the receipt.
How many T-shirts do you need?
We don't have any small sizes.
Here is your change: six dollars.
Do you have any medium sizes?
Excuse me, I think the change is wrong.
